prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: نتائج الانتخابات حسب الدائرة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "الدائرة" spans 1 col × 2 row; "المرشح أ" spans 2 col × 1 row; "المرشح ب" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "الدائرة" · longest unbreakable word 44px · one-line width 115px
  col 2: header "المرشح أ › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 51px · one-line width 51px
  col 3: header "المرشح أ › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 4: header "المرشح ب › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 51px · one-line width 51px
  col 5: header "المرشح ب › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"Header labels intact and all figures sit on one line, but the district column is a touch narrow: 'دائرة المفرق الأولى' and 'دائرة الزرقاء الأولى' break into three short stacks while the numeric columns carry visible slack, so row headers read choppily."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Numeric columns are wide with generous dead space beside each figure, while the row-header column is squeezed so almost every district wraps to three lines; scanning a row as a unit is harder than it needs to be, though nothing breaks."},"C":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Very similar to B: the four value columns absorb more width than the numbers need, leaving the district names stacked over three lines; headers and figures remain legible, so it is workable but wasteful."},"D":{"grade":"bad","why":"The candidate columns are too narrow: 'الأصوات' is broken mid-word into 'الأصوا / ت' in both header groups, and the value columns are tight around the numbers, giving a broken, unfinished look to the most important header level."},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Best balance: the district column is widest of the set (one name fits on a single line, others on two), the four numeric columns stay just wide enough for '18,420' and '13,905', headers sit intact on one line, and leftover white space is minimal."},"F":{"grade":"bad","why":"Same failure as D, worse felt: 'الأصوات' splits mid-word in both header groups, and the narrow value columns crowd the figures while the row-header column is comparatively wide, so the hierarchy looks inverted."}},"best":["E"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Differences between A, B and C are small at this rendering scale; I am inferring relative widths from wrap behaviour and whitespace rather than exact pixel values, and D/F differ mainly in the header word-break rather than number fit."}
